3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the plaintiffs are the successive heirs of Herajtullah, one of the original owners of CS Khatian Nos.384/1614 under Chourhash Mouza, some lands of the said mouza were sold in auction in Money Execution Case No.1417 of 1925 and Delbar Sheikh, original plaintiff No.1 and one Asgar Sheikh purchased the said lands in auction and took delivery of possession through Court. The remaining 2/3rd portion of the said land was purchased by Asgar Alt Sheikh from the heirs of Abu Sheikh. The plaintiffs got 7(seven) annas and 3(three) pies share in Khatian Nos.348 and 1614 and .15 acre in Khatian No.305. In this way, they have been possessing 1.18 acres land. Abdul Gani, son of Asgar Sheikh, transferred his share to the predecessors of the defendants who are men of disparate character. The plaintiffs requested the defendants to make an amicable partition of the suit lands which they refused. Hence, the plaintiffs instituted the suit. 

 14. The case of defendant that the suit land appertaining to CS Khatian Nos.384/1614 originally belongs to Heraz Sheikh, Benode Sheikh, Panchu Sheikh and Khoka Sheikh who failed to pay rent and surrendered the jama in favour of their landlord in the years 1932/1933AD. Ext-3 certified copy of suit register (as it appears from the judgment of the trial Court) shows that Ex-Landlord filed rent suit being No.3743 on 19.04.1343AD against Delbar Sheikh, son of late Benode Sheikh for rent due from 1346 to 1349 BS. One question may put forth to the effect that if the rent was due for the period from 1346 to 1349 BS that would be happened in the English year 1943AD in that case how the tenants would have surrendered the land in dispute in favour of their landlord in the years 1930-1933AD. On perusal of the aforementioned date and year, it appears that the alleged fact of surrender the land of suit jama in favour of landlord and thereafter taken fresh settlement in favour of Abiron and Zahuron appears to be inconsistent and remained not proved. With a view to prove such settlement, the case was sent back on remand in spite of that the defendant took no positive step and as such, the alleged fresh settlement remains unproved. Not only that "the tenancy right of the heirs of CS tenant remained in force and not extinguished" this fact has been recognized by the predecessor of the defendant, Najir Sheikh who purchased certain portion of land from the admitted heir of CS tenant. 

 No. 2266. We have perused the recital of kabala dated 22.05.1959. From the schedule of the same, it is seen that Plot Nos.2201, 2202 and 2206 have been inserted there but there is no existence of Plot No.2266 wherein the homontand of the defendant has been situated But the disputed CS Khatian being No. 16/14 shows that Plot Nos. 2201, 2202 and 2266 are being inserted there. From the plaint, it revealed that the present plaintiff-appellant prayed for effecting partition in respect of suit land appertaining to Plot Nos.2201, 2202, 2204 and 2266. As a result of which, it can be said that predecessor of contesting defendant has purchased certain portion of land from the suit Khatian which has been inherited by the contesting defendant. Now the learned Advocate for the present appellant (plain-tiff) argued that the defendant is liable to evicted from the house since they have acquired no right, title in Plot No.2266.
